title: Symmetrical and ...e6 Lines
intro: Black holds the centre with ...e6 or copies the bishop move with ...Bf5. Stay solid with e3, Bd3 and Nbd2.
variation: d2d4 d7d5 g1f3 g8f6 c1f4 e7e6, d2d4 d7d5 g1f3 g8f6 c1f4 c8f5

lessons.title: Meeting 3...e6
lessons.summary: Develop e3, Bg3 and Nbd2 against Black's solid set-up.

steps.text: Black often skips ...c5 at first and defends d5 calmly with 3...e6.
Support d4 and open the path for your light-squared bishop.
steps.ifRight: Now White develops cleanly with Bd3, Nbd2 and c3.

steps.text: Black challenges the diagonal with 4...Bd6.
Keep your bishop on the b1-h7 diagonal.
steps.ifWrong: Play 5.Bg3 so Black cannot trade for free.
steps.ifRight: If Black takes on g3, hxg3 opens your rook's file.

steps.text: Black castles: 5...O-O.
Bring out your queen's knight without blocking the c-pawn.
steps.hint: Develop the b1 knight to d2.
steps.ifWrong: Play 6.Nbd2, keeping c3 free for a pawn.
steps.ifRight: Next come Bd3, c3 and castling.

steps.text: Here Black played 4...Be7 instead of 4...Bd6. Continue your London development.
steps.hint: Develop the queen's knight to d2 or the bishop to d3.
steps.ifWrong: Play 5.Nbd2 (or 5.Bd3) to build the London set-up.
steps.ifRight: Both Nbd2 and Bd3 lead to a harmonious position.

lessons.title: Meeting 3...Bf5
lessons.summary: Challenge Black's bishop with Bd3 and recapture with Qxd3.

steps.text: Black mirrors your bishop move with 3...Bf5.
Stick to your set-up and support d4.
steps.ifRight: Now you are ready to challenge Black's f5 bishop.

steps.text: Black plays 4...e6, mirroring your pawn structure.
Offer a bishop trade that brings your queen into the game.
steps.hint: Put your light-squared bishop opposite Black's f5 bishop.
steps.ifWrong: Play 5.Bd3 to challenge Black's active bishop.
steps.ifRight: If Black trades on d3, your queen recaptures actively.

steps.text: Black accepts the trade: 5...Bxd3.
Recapture with the queen so your pawn structure stays clean.
steps.hint: Take with the queen, not the c-pawn.
steps.ifWrong: Play 6.Qxd3 to keep your c-pawn ready for c3 or c4.
steps.ifRight: White develops Nbd2, c3 and castles easily.

feedback.c2d3: 6.cxd3 creates a backward d-pawn and blocks your c-file ideas. Recapture with the queen.

steps.text: Black reinforces d5 with 6...c6. Continue developing your queenside.
steps.hint: Develop the knight to d2 or castle.
steps.ifRight: White has a comfortable edge in development and space.

lessons.title: Meeting 2...c5
lessons.summary: Play 3.c3 first to keep d4 firm before Bf4.

steps.text: Sometimes Black skips 2...Nf6 and hits d4 immediately with 2...c5.
Keep the centre firm before bringing the bishop out.
steps.ifWrong: Play 3.c3 so you can meet ...cxd4 with cxd4.
steps.ifRight: With d4 solidly defended, Bf4 comes next.

feedback.c1f4: 3.Bf4 lets Black trade 3...cxd4 4.Nxd4 and gain time against your knight.

steps.text: Black develops with 3...Nc6.
Now bring your dark-squared bishop out before playing e3.
steps.ifWrong: Play 4.Bf4: this transposes into the normal London lines.

steps.text: What if Black takes on d4 right after 3.c3?
Recapture with the c-pawn and keep a strong centre.
steps.ifWrong: Play 4.cxd4 to keep a central pawn on d4 and open the c-file.
steps.ifRight: Then Bf4, e3 and Nc3 give White active piece play.
